resolutions.reason: The mark under the ḥet is a T-shaped qamats, the same shape as the qamats under the kaf of כָל just before it. It is not a flat bar (pataḥ). This reverses the earlier tentative change to חַי.
A pataḥ bar is clearly printed under the Rashi alef. It is a point, not ink noise.
Same pataḥ under the Rashi alef as in the first rubric.

Each word's visible mark was compared with the candidate. Each candidate accent has a mark on the matching letter, in the matching upper or lower position. Clearly identified by shape: geresh over the ʿayin of הַשְּׁבִיעִ֜י, revia dot over the ḥet of לַחֹ֗דֶשׁ, two upper marks on קֹ֙דֶשׁ֙ (double pashta), the etnaḥta wedge under the shin of תַֽעֲשׂ֑וּ and under the second אֶחָ֑ד, the silluq bar in לָכֶֽם:, the double pashta on נִיחֹ֙חַ֙, and the zaqef over לַֽיְיָ֔. Lower conjunctives (munaḥ, merkha, tevir, darga, mahpakh) are on the expected letters; their exact shapes are only partly distinct. No mark differing from the candidate was found.
There is a single dot (ḥiriq) under the kaf, with no horizontal bar.
No separate ḥolam is visible beside the lamed head. The only dot there is the shin dot on the following ש. The tentative reading stands.
The pataḥ under the lamed, the two-dot sheva under the first yod and the qamats under the second yod are all present.
There is a sheva (two vertical dots) under the vav, which has no shuruq dot in it, and a qamats under the sin.
Same as the first: sheva under the vav and qamats under the sin, before לְחַטָּאת.
There is a horizontal pataḥ bar under the bet, not a ḥiriq dot. The dagesh in the shin is listed separately under remaining_uncertainties.
There is a third glyph after the two vavs. It is shaped like ḥet, which is how this font prints the Rashi alef (compare דיא and זאגט). So the word reads וואה, not ווה.
The last glyph is the ḥet-shaped Rashi alef, the same shape as in זאגט. It is not a Rashi he.
The middle letter matches the ג in זאגט on the same line. It does not match the ז that begins זאגט.
The mark under the mem is the same flat bar as in הַשָּׁמַיִם at the end of the line above. No qamats is visible.
There is no dot inside the pe's bowl, and the qamats is below it.
The sheva is visible under the first yod in הֵן לַיְיָ.
The medial kaf carries a qamats, and the word ends with a descending final ך with a sheva inside it. The sequence כְךָ is not printed.
